messages:
maria: Noticing a pattern: a small subset of websocket sessions get a mid-connection route switch after an opportunistic TLS renegotiate. Console shows short double-token spikes and a 'route change' annotation in traces.

dave: Do we have logs showing the header flip?

maria: example: 'X-Socket-Fingerprint: s=aa1' then after renegotiate 's=bb2' but conn_id and session_token unchanged.

olga: Probable cause: edge proxy recomputes fingerprint on resumed handshake. It then returns a different route hint.

kevin: Billing/quotas treat that as a new route and attributes tokens to the new shard, causing tiny duplicate charges.

maria: Proposal: short-term proxy rule: if conn_id and session token are identical, and fingerprint changed within 15s, keep original route and emit telemetry tag 'fingerprint.jitter.suppressed'.

olga: Implementation note: we can add orig_route to routing context and a last_fp_ts. If new_fp && (now - last_fp_ts) < 15s && conn_id==orig_conn -> route=orig_route.

dave: Console: add flag to session view to show when jitter was suppressed so support isn't blind to it.

kevin: I'll add a billing dedupe step: ignore token attributions when 'fingerprint.jitter.suppressed' tag present within 20s window.

deploy-bot: plan: sticky-fingerprint canary in us-east-1 for 12h (flag=fp_sticky_v1).

maria: owners: @olga proxy, @kevin billing, @dave console. Small RFC + canary checklist incoming.

kevin: also sample 0.1% of suppressed cases and force re-route to check false positives.

maria: agreed. we'll monitor 'suppressed.false_positive' metric during canary.
